description:
Read the turnover a French micro-entrepreneur declares to the URSSAF for one period, from the bank receipts of the period and the invoices they settle, split by activity. Use it to prepare the URSSAF turnover declaration ("déclare mon chiffre d'affaires URSSAF", "what turnover do I declare this quarter"). It reads only and stores nothing.

Pass `period_start` and `period_end` (YYYY-MM-DD), the first and last day of the declaration period: a month or a quarter, at most 366 days.

**`totals`** gives one entry per activity (`goods`, `services_bic`, `services_bnc`) in EUR. `net_amount` is net of VAT: it is the turnover to declare. `gross_only_amount` is money whose VAT share Well cannot tell (a receipt with no invoice while the company charges VAT): never add it to `net_amount`, and say that the amount includes VAT. State each total with its activity. Never add up amounts yourself.

**`questions`** lists the receipts that wait for the person's answer before they count, each with a `reason`: `no_invoice` (no invoice settles it), `operation_nature_unstated` (its invoice does not say goods or services), `invoice_side_unconfirmed` (Well cannot prove the company issued its invoice), `allocation_not_in_receipt_currency`. Ask one question per `transaction_id` (one receipt can list several parts, and one answer settles them all): is it a sale of goods, a service, or not turnover? Save the answer with `well_set_transaction_category` (decision `user_choice`): "Services & implementation revenue" for a service, and a category that is not revenue (for example "Inter-account transfer (same entity)" or "Loan drawdowns & repayments") for money that is not turnover. For a sale of goods while `micro_activity_regime` is `goods`, save "Subscription & product revenue": under that profile it counts as goods. Then read again: the next read counts the answer and never asks it again. Under any other profile no category records a sale of goods: say the amount stays outside the totals until the payment is matched to its sales invoice. Under those profiles "Subscription & product revenue" does not answer the question, and "Uncategorised / suspense" never does: a receipt filed under one of them is still asked.

**`services_unassigned`** is service money while the profile names no service activity (`micro_activity_regime` is `goods` or not set). Ask once whether the services are commercial or craft services (BIC) or a liberal profession (BNC). When the profile says `goods`, saving a service activity replaces it: say that the profile then names the services activity (goods receipts still count as goods), and save only after the person agrees. Save `micro_activity_regime` with `well_upsert_accounting_settings`, and read again.

**`unsigned_receipts`** counts the rows of the period whose direction (money in or money out) Well does not know, such as the lines of an uploaded statement: none of them is in the totals. Some can be payments out, so call them rows whose direction is unknown, never receipts, and say how many there are. `not_turnover` counts money the records say is not turnover (a supplier refund, a credit note, a category that is not revenue). `other_currency` lists receipts in another currency: they are not converted and not counted.

**`sources`** gives each bank source with `fresh_enough`. For an `installation` source with `fresh_enough: false` and `syncable: true`, call `well_request_sync` with its `workspace_connector_id`, then read again, or say the bank copy dates from `synced_at`. `syncable: false` means the installation belongs to another workspace: never request its sync, and say the bank copy dates from `synced_at`. Its `workspace_connector_id` names it only: no tool of this workspace takes it. For a `statement` source with `fresh_enough: false`, say the statements stop at `covered_to` (NULL: they do not cover the first day of the period, or they stop before it) and ask for the statement that covers the rest of the period. An `uncovered_account` source is an account of the company that no connected bank serves and no imported statement covers: its receipts are missing from the totals, so name the account and ask the person to connect its bank or send its statements. `unsourced_receipts` counts receipts of the period whose bank was disconnected or that came from no bank and no statement: say the bank behind them is not connected. A receipt the person entered in Well is never unsourced. `sources_truncated: true` means the period has more sources than one read lists.

**`all_sources_fresh_enough`** is true only when every source is fresh enough, the list is whole, no receipt is unsourced and the period has ended. Never present a total as complete while it is false. With no source at all it is false: say Well reads no bank for the period. `own_account_scope_unreadable: true` also makes it false: Well could not list the company's accounts, so say the turnover may miss an account. `period_ended: false` means the period is still open: the totals are the turnover so far, not the amount to declare, so say so and do not request a sync for it.

**`totals_complete`** is true only when the totals are the whole turnover to declare: `all_sources_fresh_enough` is true, no row's direction is unknown, no question waits, `services_unassigned` is empty, no receipt is in another currency and no total has a `gross_only_amount`. Present the totals as the amount to declare only when it is true; otherwise say what is still missing.

`status`: `too_many_receipts` means the period holds more receipts than one read takes: no total is given, never a partial one. `unsupported_jurisdiction`: the accounting country is not France. `invalid_period`: fix the dates. `failed`: the read failed and the turnover is unknown, never zero.

When the token authorizes one workspace, call this directly — no workspace call is needed first. When it authorizes several, this read will not guess which one you mean: pass `workspace_id` on the call.

conversation_id.description: The conversation id returned by the previous Well result, in its meta under well/conversation_id, in its structuredContent, or in its JSON text block. Pass it back on every call in the same conversation, including a call a card makes, so the chosen workspace and the earlier answers still apply. It decides the conversation on its own: nothing the host states about the session replaces it. Omit it only on the first call of a conversation.

period_end.description: Last day of the declaration period, YYYY-MM-DD.

period_start.description: First day of the declaration period, YYYY-MM-DD.

workspace_id.description: Target workspace. Omit when the token authorizes one workspace. Required when it authorizes several: this read reports one workspace's own figures and will not choose which.

workspace_scope.description: Restrict this call to the family: the token's primary workspace plus the company workspaces under it that you are a member of. Unrelated authorized workspaces drop out of the read; row reads merge across the family, while a per-workspace figure still reports exactly one workspace.

name: well_get_micro_turnover

conversation_id.description: The conversation this result belongs to. Pass it back as the conversation_id argument on every later Well call in the same conversation.

conversation_id_note.description: Present only when the server opened a fresh lane, stating that no choice recorded earlier was read.

conversation_id_source.description: Where the conversation id came from: the host's own request meta, the caller's argument, or a fresh lane the server opened.

newly_connected.description: Tools that connected to this workspace since the last result and that no session was told about yet, oldest first. Present only when at least one tool is new. The connected-line rule says when to tell an entry; when it does, one line per entry, in the person's language: "<name> is connected.". Never fold several entries into one sentence. Each entry comes back once, on one result only: never repeat its line later.

resolved_workspace.description: The workspace that answered, when the caller named none and the token authorizes several.

title: Get micro-entrepreneur turnover
